Explicit missingness and acceptance boundary

Rights: Figshare dataset version 2 and its downloadable files are CC BY 4.0; attribution and change notice are retained.

Admission: One source-local population profile remains admitted. Selected local source information uses 25 original workbooks: 23 existing experiment-family workbooks with 2,115 source observations and 220 within-table condition groups, plus two separate NaV inhibition workbooks with 84 worksheet measurement rows. The full retained original XLSX inventory is 26, including INa.xlsx not selected by the existing family adapter. These file and row counts are not a unique physical-cell or animal denominator and add no type or exact-cell roster. Four source conflicts stay quarantined; the separate NaV label/protocol discrepancies remain visible. No geometry, registration, global per-cell or cross-workbook NaV pairing, cross-experiment-family join, or link to the separate PKD2L1 SBF-SEM study is created.

Global Cell Roster · UNAVAILABLE: Generic cell labels are reused across regions and experiment families; no global stable cell ID exists.
Raw Electrophysiology Traces · UNAVAILABLE: No raw ABF/pClamp traces, acquisition timestamps or recording-file identifiers are deposited.
Single Cell Morphology And Internal Structure · UNAVAILABLE: No raw microscopy volume, segmentation, SWC, EM stack, organelle mesh or stable same-cell morphology object is deposited.
Atlas Registration · NOT ESTABLISHED: No source coordinate transform or atlas registration is admitted.
Cross Source Identity · NOT ESTABLISHED: Shared PKD2L1 identity does not join this functional profile to the separate SBF-SEM paper, morphology records or transcriptomic records.

UPG-168 · P0 · Internal Microdetail
Research Watch — Biologically Relevant PKD2L1 VEM Study Lacks Deposited Source Objects

Monitor the PKD2L1 cerebrospinal-fluid-contacting-neuron SBF-SEM study as the closest biologically qualifying mouse-spinal interneuron internal-detail candidate found. The paper identifies GABAergic PKD2L1-positive spinal interneurons and reports targeted same-cell serial block-face EM, but no stable public raw stack, section series, segmentation, mesh or source-to-figure object manifest was located. Publication images and measurements cannot substitute for downloadable calibrated voxels or establish a reusable cell object. Admission remains blocked until the authors or a repository deposit stable object IDs, raw calibrated 3D pixels, same-cell membrane/cell segmentation and labelled nucleus, organelle or synapse objects, coordinate/voxel metadata, bytes, cryptographic checksums, object-level reuse rights and raw-versus-mask overlay QC. Until then the runtime renders zero PKD2L1 geometry or internals and makes no atlas registration, complete-cell, prevalence or general-interneuron claim

UPG-172 · P2 · Electrophysiology
Completed

Add exactly one source-local PKD2L1 CSF-contacting-neuron functional profile from Figshare version `10.6084/m9.figshare.29430869.v2`. The deterministic contract records the official CC BY 4.0 92-file / 1,848,613-byte inventory and pins seven key objects by file ID, bytes, publisher MD5 and locally verified SHA-256. It preserves 3–6-week cervical/thoracic/lumbar scope; exact firing-pattern denominators (C N=10/n=21, T N=12/n=23, L N=9/n=21); paper N=191/n=659 versus 654 deposited passive-property rows; N=25/n=125 resting-potential observations; and exact anatomy FOV/cell totals. Four conflicts remain quarantined: paper-versus-workbook firing p values, incomplete/no-denominator firing-location coverage, 659-versus-654 passive-property rows, and thoracic 6-week distance n=478 versus FOV n=457. The deposit contains observation tables but no globally stable cell key: tonic/single-spike, segment, quadrant and experiment-family rows stay nested evidence rather than new types. The UI exposes observed cohort/experiment-family electrophysiology while retaining zero raw traces, microscopy volume, morphology, geometry, internal objects, atlas registration, whole-deposit per-cell join or link to the separate UPG-168 SBF-SEM study
